paper: Angrist & Krueger (1991), 'Does Compulsory School Attendance Affect Schooling and Earnings?', QJE 106(4):979-1014, DOI 10.2307/2937954

environment.gpu_model: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (x4) - not needed; this is a CPU/econometrics replication

data.source: NEW7080/NEW7080.dta (Angrist Data Archive), 1,063,634 obs x 27 vars

table_IV_1970_1920_29.published_comparison: matches AK Table IV (OLS ~0.080, Wald col2 ~0.077, col8 ~0.101)

table_V_1980_1930_39.published_comparison: matches AK Table V (col1 0.071, col2 0.089, col6 0.081)

table_VI_1980_1940_49.published_comparison: matches AK Table VI (col1 0.057, col2 0.055, col4 0.095, col8 0.078); QOB significant in wage eq for this cohort

table_III_wald.published_comparison: matches AK Table III (Panel A Wald 0.0715/OLS 0.0801; Panel B Wald 0.1020/OLS 0.0709)

table_I_education_outcomes.pattern: Q1 negative for total education & HS graduation in both cohorts; near-zero for college/masters/doctoral (as expected)

figures.fig4_q1_below_MA: 18 of 19 birth-years show Q1 education below the MA(+2,-2) prediction
figures.pattern: recurring first-quarter education dip; rising age-earnings profile for younger cohort that flattens for older cohort; Q1 births earn slightly less

reproducibility_verdict: REPRODUCED. All 7 steps ran to completion at full scale (no downsizing). The three IV/TSLS regression tables (IV, V, VI), the Table III Wald estimates, the Table I detrended QOB-on-education regressions, and the Figure I/II/IV/V descriptive series all reproduce the published Angrist-Krueger (1991) results closely. Only documented limitation: the shipped extract spans birth years 1930-1949 only, so the 1950s panels of Figures III/IV are not reproducible from this data (noted in the plan).
notes_on_fixes: No code errors required patching; the three Stata .do files were ported to R (reg->lm, ivregress 2sls->AER::ivreg) and hardcoded Windows paths replaced with the relative dataset path. The 'some instrumental variables are collinear' ivreg warning is benign (AGEQ/AGEQSQ overlap with the YOB-dummy + QOB-interaction instrument set) and matches Stata's ivregress handling; results are unaffected and match the paper.
